title: Complement Consumption Patterns: Reading C3, C4 and the Snapshot Problem
summary: Learn what C3, C4 and factor B levels each report, why an antigenic level is a snapshot of production minus consumption, how to read low C3 with low or normal C4 (lupus versus C3 nephritic factor), and why a normal level neither proves function nor rules out activation.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 48 Hits 7 (SLE complement), 10 (C3 nephritic factor), 12 (pathway-activity pattern), 14 (snapshot) and Traps 1, 2 and 4, checked against Ekdahl 2018, Ayano 2023 and the C3 glomerulopathy consensus report (Pickering 2013), all read as Europe PMC full text. Two qualifications are taught and flagged: “quiescent SLE → normal C4” does not hold reliably (persistent low levels in remission and low C4 gene copy number), and factor B is not a reliable discriminator (it can stay near normal with C3NeF and is consumed in lupus flares). Not verified, so not taught: the reviewer’s “half-life ≥10×” for the C3NeF-stabilised convertase, and the rheumatoid-arthritis serum-versus-synovial-fluid example.

objectives: State which pathways use C3, C4 and factor B, and what an antigenic C3 or C4 assay detects.
Explain why a complement level is a snapshot of production minus consumption, and why split products are more sensitive markers of activation.
Interpret low C3 with low C4 versus low C3 with normal C4, including C3 nephritic factor and the limits of factor B and C4 in lupus.

scenes.title: Three complement panels
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three serum complement panels arrive. (1) A woman with lupus and a new rash: C3 low, C4 low. (2) A child with blood in the urine: C3 low, C4 normal, C3 nephritic factor positive. (3) A lupus patient with active nephritis on biopsy: C3 normal, C4 normal. Question token: “Which pathway, and does normal mean quiet?”

cues.text: Three complement panels arrive. A woman with lupus and a new rash has a low C3 and a low C4.
A child with blood in the urine has a low C3, a normal C4, and a positive C3 nephritic factor. A third patient has active lupus nephritis, yet normal C3 and C4.
Which pathway is being used up in each, and does a normal result mean complement is quiet?

props.label: Which pathway? Does normal mean quiet?

scenes.title: What each number measures
scenes.altText: Schematic: three pathway lanes converge on C3. Card C3: shared by all three pathways (the common substrate of every C3 convertase). Card C4: used only by the classical and lectin pathways. Card factor B: used by the alternative pathway. Card “Antigenic assay”: nephelometry or turbidimetry with polyclonal antibodies; anti-C3c antibodies recognise intact C3 AND its fragments C3b, iC3b and C3c, so the result is a protein concentration with no information on activation state. Card “Functional assay”: hemolytic CH50/AH50 need every component in the pathway to be active.

cues.text: Each number reports a different piece. C3 is shared by all three pathways: every C3 convertase cleaves it.
C4 is used only by the classical and lectin pathways, and factor B by the alternative pathway.

Routine C3 and C4 are antigenic assays, usually nephelometry or turbidimetry. Antibodies against the C3c part recognise intact C3 and its fragments, C3b, iC3b and C3c, so the result is an amount of protein, not proof that it works.
Function needs a functional test. A hemolytic assay lyses red cells only if every component along the pathway is active.

props.title: Antigenic (nephelometry)
lines: Anti-C3c sees C3, C3b, iC3b, C3c

scenes.title: A level is a snapshot
scenes.altText: Balance diagram: serum level = production minus consumption. In vivo, activated complement fragments are taken up by receptor-bearing cells (leukocytes, Kupffer cells), so activation shows up as consumption. Production card: synthesis can rise too (the acute-phase response increases production; C3 is also much higher in obesity), so the intact level alone is a poor gauge of activation. Split-product card: iC3b, C3d,g and C4d are made only by activation and are not raised by the acute-phase response; because C3 turns over continuously, activation is judged as a ratio such as C3d,g/C3. SLE card: normal complement levels during active disease, and persistent low levels in remission, are both often seen.

cues.text: A complement level is a snapshot of a balance: what the liver makes minus what activation uses up. In the body, activated fragments are cleared by receptor-bearing cells, so activation shows as consumption.
Production can rise too. The acute-phase response increases synthesis, and C3 is much higher in obesity, so the level alone is a poor gauge of activation.

Split products, such as iC3b, C3d,g and C4d, are made only by activation and are not raised by acute-phase production. Because C3 turns over all the time, activation is judged as a ratio, such as C3d,g to C3.
In lupus this matters: normal C3 and C4 during active disease, and persistently low levels in remission, are both often seen.

scenes.title: Reading the pattern
scenes.altText: Pattern table. Low C3 + low C4 → classical (or lectin) pathway activation, the usual lupus picture; in a lupus flare C3, C4 and factor B are consumed, classical hemolytic function falls and activation products peak. Low C3 + normal C4 → alternative pathway activation, for example C3 glomerulopathy: C3 nephritic factor (C3NeF) is an autoantibody that stabilises the alternative C3 convertase C3bBb, causing profound C3 consumption; detecting it supports C3 glomerulopathy, in particular dense deposit disease. Factor B caveat: may fall in uncontrolled alternative activation, but in C3NeF disease can stay more or less unchanged. Low C4 alone, persistently, in lupus: consider a low C4 gene copy number. Hook answers: (1) classical; (2) alternative, C3 glomerulopathy work-up; (3) normal levels do not rule out activation; split products help.

cues.text: Read C3 with its company. Low C3 with low C4 points to the classical or lectin pathway, the usual lupus picture, where immune complexes start the cascade at C1.

Low C3 with a normal C4 points to the alternative pathway. In C3 glomerulopathy, C3 nephritic factor is an autoantibody that stabilises the alternative C3 convertase, C3bBb, and C3 is used up. A positive result supports C3 glomerulopathy, especially dense deposit disease.

Factor B is a weaker clue: it can fall in alternative activation, but may stay near normal with C3 nephritic factor, and lupus flares can consume it too. A persistently low C4 alone may simply reflect fewer C4 genes.
Back to the hook: panel one is classical, panel two is alternative and needs a C3 glomerulopathy work-up, and panel three shows that normal levels do not rule out activation.

props.title: Hook answers
lines: 3 Normal does not rule out activation

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Normal C3 and C4 rule out complement consumption” (✓ a level is production minus consumption; normal levels occur in active lupus; activation products are more sensitive); “Low C3 means alternative pathway activation” (✓ check C4: low C3 with low C4 is classical or lectin; low C3 with normal C4 is alternative); “A normal antigenic C3 means C3 is working” (✓ antigenic assays count intact C3 and its fragments; function needs a functional assay).

cues.text: Trap one: normal C3 and C4 rule out consumption. No: a level is production minus use, and normal levels are often seen in active lupus.
Trap two: a low C3 means the alternative pathway. No: check C4. Low C3 with low C4 is classical or lectin activation.
Trap three: a normal antigenic C3 means C3 works. No: the assay counts protein, fragments included. Function needs a functional test.

scenes.title: The balance, not the receipts
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “C3 and C4 are a bank BALANCE: deposits (synthesis) minus spending (activation). A healthy balance can hide heavy spending; the RECEIPTS (split products) show the spending. C4 is the classical lane’s card: if C4 is spent too, the classical lane was shopping.” Tokens: balance = C3/C4 level · receipts = split products · C4 = classical card. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: C3 and C4 are a bank balance, deposits minus spending. A healthy balance can hide heavy spending; the receipts, the split products, show it. And C4 is the classical lane’s card: if C4 is spent too, the classical lane was shopping.

Where it breaks: a low C4 can be inherited, from fewer C4 genes, not spending; receipts can be printed in the tube if the sample is mishandled, so activation products need careful collection; and factor B is not a reliable card for the alternative lane.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: Low C4 can be genetic (fewer C4 genes)

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “C3 ↓ + C4 ↓ = classical/lectin · C3 ↓ + C4 normal = alternative (C3NeF)”, “Level = made − used · antigenic ≠ function · normal does not rule out activation”.

cues.text: Read C3 together with C4, low together for the classical or lectin pathway and low C3 alone for the alternative pathway, and remember that an antigenic level is a snapshot of production minus use, so a normal value neither proves function nor rules out activation.

props.label: C3↓ C4↓ = classical/lectin · C3↓ C4 normal = alternative
Level = made − used · amount ≠ function · normal ≠ quiet

explanation.what: Plain language: the lab usually measures how much C3 and C4 protein is in the blood. A low amount suggests the system is being used up, and which pieces are low hints at which pathway is running. But the amount depends on how much the body makes as well as how much it uses, and the test counts broken pieces too. Scientific terms: C3, C4, factor B, antigenic (immunochemical) assay, nephelometry, turbidimetry, functional hemolytic assay (CH50, AH50), consumption, acute-phase response, split products (iC3b, C3d,g, C4d), C3d,g/C3 ratio, C3 nephritic factor (C3NeF), alternative C3 convertase C3bBb, C3 glomerulopathy, dense deposit disease, C4 gene copy number, serologically active clinically quiescent lupus.
explanation.why: C3 is cleaved by every pathway, C4 only by the classical and lectin pathways, and factor B by the alternative pathway, so the pattern of low components points to a pathway. Activated fragments are cleared in vivo, so activation appears as consumption, synthesis can also rise (in the acute-phase response, and C3 in obesity), and normal levels are often seen in active lupus, while polyclonal anti-C3c assays also count fragments, so a normal level does not prove intact, working C3 or an absence of activation.
explanation.measure: Antigenic C3/C4: nephelometry or turbidimetry with polyclonal antibodies (anti-C3c recognises C3, C3b, iC3b and C3c). Function: hemolytic CH50 (classical) and AH50 (alternative). Activation: split products by neo-epitope antibody assays (or, for C3d,g, precipitation of larger C3 forms before immunoassay), interpreted as a ratio to C3 (for example C3d,g/C3). Samples: EDTA plasma for components and activation products, serum for function, kept cold and frozen at −80 °C.
explanation.differs: Low C3 + low C4 (classical or lectin activation, lupus) vs low C3 + normal C4 (alternative activation, C3NeF and C3 glomerulopathy); antigenic amount vs functional activity; intact component level vs split-product ratio; low C4 from consumption vs low C4 gene copy number.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: name the pathway from a C3/C4 pattern, link C3NeF to low C3 with normal C4 and dense deposit disease, recognise that a normal C3 or C4 does not exclude active consumption, and that antigenic assays do not measure function.

comparisons.title: Classical vs alternative consumption
comparisons.distinguisher: C4: used by the classical and lectin pathways only.

comparisons.title: Antigenic level vs function and activation
comparisons.distinguisher: How much is there vs whether it works or is being activated.

mnemonic.text: C3 and C4 are a bank BALANCE: deposits (synthesis) minus spending (activation). A healthy balance can hide heavy spending; the RECEIPTS (split products) show it. C4 is the classical lane’s card: if C4 is spent too, the classical lane was shopping.
mnemonic.explanation: Links level, production, consumption and split products, and uses C4 to separate the pathways.
mnemonic.limitation: A low C4 can be inherited (low C4 gene copy number) rather than consumed; split products can form in a mishandled sample, so they need careful collection; factor B is not a reliable marker of alternative-pathway activation.

analogyLimitations: The bank-balance analogy ignores half-lives and differences between assays.
takeaway: Read C3 together with C4, low together for the classical or lectin pathway and low C3 alone for the alternative pathway, and remember that an antigenic level is a snapshot of production minus use, so a normal value neither proves function nor rules out activation.

questions.stem: A child with hematuria has a low serum C3, a normal C4 and a positive C3 nephritic factor. Which interpretation fits best?

options.text: Alternative pathway dysregulation, consistent with C3 glomerulopathy
options.rationale: Correct. C3 nephritic factor stabilises the alternative C3 convertase, C3bBb, consuming C3 while C4 stays normal; it supports C3 glomerulopathy, especially dense deposit disease.

options.text: Classical pathway activation by immune complexes
options.rationale: Incorrect. Classical activation consumes C4 as well as C3; here C4 is normal.
Incorrect. C4 is normal, and C4 deficiency would not explain a low C3 with a positive C3 nephritic factor.
Incorrect. C1-inhibitor deficiency typically lowers C4, not C3 alone, and C3 nephritic factor is unrelated to it.

questions.stem: A nephelometric C3 assay uses polyclonal antibodies against the C3c portion of C3. What does a normal result tell you?

options.text: The amount of C3-containing protein, including fragments such as C3b, iC3b and C3c
options.rationale: Correct. Anti-C3c antibodies recognise intact C3 and its C3c-containing fragments, so the result gives concentration but no information on activation state or function.
Incorrect. Function needs a functional assay, such as a hemolytic test.

options.text: That no complement activation is taking place
options.rationale: Incorrect. Normal levels are often seen during active disease, as in lupus; activation products reflect activation more sensitively.

options.text: That the classical pathway is intact
options.rationale: Incorrect. A single component level cannot show that every classical component works; CH50 assesses the whole pathway.

questions.stem: A patient with lupus has active nephritis, yet serum C3 and C4 are within the reference interval. Which statement is most accurate?

options.text: Normal levels do not rule out activation; split products such as the C3d,g/C3 ratio reflect activation more sensitively
options.rationale: Correct. A level is production minus consumption, normal levels are often seen in active lupus, and split products are made only by activation.

options.text: Complement cannot be involved, so the nephritis is not lupus-related
options.rationale: Incorrect. Normal C3 and C4 do not exclude complement activation or lupus nephritis.

options.text: The normal C4 proves the alternative pathway is responsible
options.rationale: Incorrect. The pattern rule applies to a low C3; normal C3 and C4 do not localise a pathway.

options.text: Repeat C3 and C4 by a different antigenic method to obtain the true value
options.rationale: Incorrect. Another antigenic method still measures amount, not activation; activation products answer the question.

claims.text: C3 is shared by all pathways; C4 is used by the classical and lectin pathways; factor B by the alternative pathway.
Antigenic (polyclonal anti-C3c) assays detect C3 and its fragments and give no information on activation or function; hemolytic assays require every component.

Activated fragments are cleared in vivo, so activation appears as consumption; synthesis can rise (acute-phase response; C3 in obesity); normal levels are often seen in active lupus; split products arise only from activation, are unaffected by acute-phase production, and are read as ratios to C3.
Low C3 + low C4 = classical or lectin activation; low C3 + normal C4 = alternative activation; factor B is an unreliable discriminator.
Lupus flares consume C3, C4 and factor B; normal levels in active disease and persistent low levels in remission are common; low C4 alone may reflect low C4 gene copy number.
C3NeF is an autoantibody that stabilises C3bBb, causing C3 consumption; detection supports C3 glomerulopathy, in particular dense deposit disease.

Reviewer details not taught: C3NeF extends convertase half-life at least 10-fold; rheumatoid arthritis with normal serum but low synovial-fluid complement; the specific mechanism that acute-phase overproduction holds C3/C4 in the normal range during active consumption (the sources read show raised synthesis and normal levels in active disease, but not this causal link).
claims.note: No open source read in this session supported these specifics.

claims.text: Scenario and panels invented; pathway lanes schematic.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 48 Hit 7 states quiescent SLE has a normal C4. Ayano 2023 reports that normal complement in active disease and persistent hypocomplementemia in remission (serologically active clinically quiescent SLE) are often observed, and that persistently low C4 alone may reflect low C4 gene copy number rather than activity (register flag rv-sle-c4-quiescent).

Ch. 48 Hit 12 and Trap 2 use factor B as a discriminator (normal in classical, low in alternative activation). Pickering 2013 does list reduced factor B among markers of alternative-pathway activation, but notes these abnormalities may vary over the disease course, and its Table 1 uses low C3 with normal C4 as the indicator. Ekdahl 2018 reports that factor B remains more or less unchanged in C3NeF-driven C3 glomerulopathy and (schematic Figure 7) is consumed with C3 and C4 during SLE exacerbations. The lesson uses C4 as the main discriminator (register flag rv-factor-b-discriminator).
